title: The Merchant, the Old Woman, and the King

keywords: tale of the merchant the crone and the king
full_text:
A wealthy merchant of Cairo entrusted a sealed leather pouch containing a magnificent ruby worth twenty thousand dinars to an old woman who lived near the Great Mosque, believing her to be an ascetic saint.

Upon his return from Mecca, he asked for his pouch; the old woman returned the leather bag, but when the merchant opened the seal, he found only a polished red glass bead in place of his ruby!

The old woman wept and shrieked, accusing the merchant of slandering a pious widow. The citizens took her part, and the merchant was driven away.

The merchant brought his suit before the Sultan. The Sultan summoned the old woman, but rather than threatening her with torture, he engaged her in pleasant conversation, offering her sweetmeats and a cup of mint tea.

While she drank, the Sultan quietly observed her hands: her fingernails were stained with green lapidary wax, and in her sleeve rested a jeweler’s brass file!

The Sultan suddenly said: 'O mother, my royal jeweler has lost his finest cutting tool; will you lend me that file in your sleeve to trim my signet ring?'

The old woman turned pale as ashes, realizing that her trade as a counterfeit gem-cutter was exposed!

The Sultan sent guards to search her cellar, where they unearthed the merchant’s real ruby, along with fifty counterfeit glass stones.

The ruby was restored to the merchant, the old woman was sentenced to repay all her victims, and the city praised the Sultan’s keen observation, which had seen through the guise of false piety.
moral: Keen judicial observation and testing subtle habits expose the craftiest thief.
